name: Matrixyl 3000
lead: Matrixyl 3000 is a branded peptide complex made by Sederma that combines palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7, and it appears in anti-wrinkle serums and creams. Users apply it to the face and around the eyes with the aim of softer lines and firmer-looking skin, since the peptides are described as signals that promote extracellular matrix remodelling.[2][3]

Its predecessor, Matrixyl (palmitoyl pentapeptide-4), was launched by Sederma in 2000; the original is a five-amino-acid peptide attached to a 16-carbon fatty chain meant to help it pass through skin lipids, and it is described as a matrikine that may activate genes involved in matrix renewal.[3]

Published work on the blend includes a 2026 permeation study that detected both peptides within layers of the stratum corneum of three volunteers and a 2026 study of palmitoyl tripeptide-1 timing alongside baicalin in fibroblasts, mice and 30 women.[2][4]

paras: The two peptides are lipid-modified fragments proposed to signal skin cells about matrix repair and inflammation. A patent application lists oligopeptide derivatives with acyl groups combined with apple extract for wrinkles, tested in 42 women aged 40 to 70 around the eyes over four weeks.[1]

A 2026 study in the International Journal of Pharmaceutics used secondary ion mass spectrometry and tape stripping in three healthy women to follow how the peptides in a Matrixyl 3000 serum moved into the stratum corneum after 0.5, 2 and 5 hours; both peptides were detected in layers of the stratum corneum but appeared to remain between cells.[2]

A 2026 Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology study modelled day-night rhythms of collagen metabolism in fibroblasts, tested daytime baicalin with nighttime palmitoyl tripeptide-1 in mice for 8 weeks, and ran a trial in 30 women using the same time-coordinated scheme.[4] A 2026 International Journal of Cosmetic Science study used knowledge-graph screening and docking to identify peptides that might raise type III collagen, then tested selected peptides in fibroblasts and ex vivo skin.[5]

No independent trial of Matrixyl 3000 itself was found. The permeation study examined its two peptides in serums on three volunteers.[2] A 30-woman clinical trial tested palmitoyl tripeptide-1 at night alongside baicalin by day, so its findings concern that regimen rather than the branded blend.[4] Wikipedia notes that the original Matrixyl's efficacy statements are tagged as needing medical citation, with some efficacy studies attributed to Sederma.[3]

card.note: Sources for this entry are thin.

quick.overview:
Matrixyl 3000 is a branded pairing of two lab-made peptides used in anti-wrinkle serums.

Independent published human data on the blend are limited.
quick.mechanism: Its peptides are proposed to signal skin cells to repair matrix and reduce inflammation; one study found they stay in the skin surface layers.
quick.risks: A cosmetic ingredient; no blend-specific safety data were found in the sources reviewed.

chain: Lipid-linked peptides applied in a serum
Peptides described as signalling matrix repair in skin
angle.text: People use serums containing the complex on the face and eye area to soften the look of wrinkles. Manufacturers and researchers describe the peptides as promoting extracellular matrix remodelling.
